planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or divisions in spring into lean, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun; established plants shrug off coastal wind, salt spray, and poor ground.

directions: Diddle-dee is the low, wiry, heather-like evergreen shrub that blankets windswept moorland across Patagonia, Tierra del Fuego, and the Falkland Islands, its tiny needle-like leaves forming dense, springy hummocks only a foot or so tall. Small pinkish flowers in spring give way to abundant red to purplish berries that ripen through summer and persist into winter, traditionally gathered by Falkland Islanders for jam, jelly, and homemade wine. It wants lean, acidic, sharply drained soil and full sun, tolerating relentless coastal wind, salt spray, and poor ground far better than rich garden beds. Propagate by rooted cuttings or division rather than seed, and avoid hot, humid summer climates where this cool-maritime species struggles.
sources: Falkland Islands Government — Native Plants of the Falklands
Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh — Flora of Tierra del Fuego
